Probabilistic Static Voltage Stability Assessment for 
Distribution Network Considering Correlated 
Renewable Energy 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Xiaoxi Huang  
State Grid East China Power 
Grid 
State Grid Corporation of China 
Shanghai, China

School of Electronic Information

Abstract—In this paper, a probabilistic static voltage stability 
assessment method is proposed to study the influence of correlated 
renewable energy and loads on static voltage stability of 
distribution network. Through non-parametric kernel density 
estimation, the probability distribution function of distributed 
renewable generation output power is obtained, and the joint 
probability distribution is established by Copula function. Based 
on the quasi-monte Carlo simulation, the samples of random input 
variables are gained, and then the distribution of load margin is 
calculated. The efficiency and accuracy of quasi-monte Carlo 
simulation is verified, and the impact of the correlation between 
distributed generation on the static voltage stability of distribution 
network is studied. Besides, the influence of distributed generation 
configuration on voltage stability is also discussed. 
Keywords—distribution network ; renewable generation ; 
uncertainty; copula function; static voltage stability 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Recently, the penetration rate of distributed generation (DG) 
in the distribution network has gradually increased, where the 
wind power and photovoltaic power generation are mainly 
used[1]. However, due to the uncertainties and correlations of the 
output of DG and loads, the static voltage stability of the 
distribution network will be affected [2]. Therefore, in order to 
guarantee the stable operation of distribution network, it is 
necessary to study the probabilistic static voltage stability 
assessment method of the distribution network considering the 
uncertainties and correlations. 
The static voltage stability analysis is based on the power 
flow equation. The load margin is obtained by calculating the 
critical point of the system static voltage stability. The common 
methods contain direct method, nonlinear programming method 
and continuous power flow method [3]. Further, considering the 
uncertainty in system, the scholars have proposed some 
probability assessment methods for static voltage stability. In 
[4], based on the point estimate method and the Cornish-Fisher 
series, a static voltage stability probability assessment method 
for the distribution network was proposed. In [3], through quasi-
monte Carlo (QMC) simulation, a probabilistic static voltage 
stability method was proposed and the influence of the 
stochastic factors such as wind power and loads on the voltage 
stability margin is studied. In [5], combining the analytical 
method and approximation method, a probability model 
considering the random characteristics of the DG output was 
established. However, in above literatures, the DG output is 
obtained according to the parametric model of random variables, 
such as the Weibull distribution of wind speed and the Beta 
distribution of solar radiation intensity. The stochastic 
distribution characteristics in some regions cannot be simply 
described by the parametric model. Therefore, it is necessary to 
apply the non-parametric estimation method to depict the 
probability distribution of the random variable. Kernel density 
estimation (KDE) is a non-parametric estimation method which 
can gain the probability distribution of random input variables[6]. 
Meanwhile, there is a certain correlation between the same type 
of DG and the load, and their influences on the static voltage 
stability of the distribution network cannot be ignored. 
In this paper, considering the uncertainties of DG output and 
loads, a probabilistic static voltage stability assessment method 
for distribution network is proposed. The probability 
distribution of DG output is generated by non-parametric KDE. 
The joint probability distribution between DGs with correlation 
is established by Copula function. Then, the samples of random 
input variables are obtained based on QMC simulation and the 
load margin is calculated by continuous power flow method. 
Through the simulation of IEEE 33-bus distribution network, the 
PDF of load margin is obtained. The efficiency and accuracy of 
QMC simulation are verified. Meanwhile, the effect of the 
correlation of DGs and loads on the static voltage stability is 
analyzed. The influence of DG configuration on improving 
voltage stability is further studied. 
II. PROBABILISTIC STATIC VOLTAGE STABILITY 
Continuous power flow is a method to analyze the system 
static voltage stability. In the distribution network, due to the 
uncertainty and correlation of DG output and loads, a 
probabilistic static voltage stability model is established based 
on the continuous power flow equation.

approximation method and analytical method. Compared with 
other methods, the Monte Carlo simulation method is robust, 
which can easily handle complex random problems. However, 
in order to obtain accurate results, MCS based on simple random 
sampling (SRS) requires a large amount of samples for repeated 
calculation which is time-consuming. Therefore, the QMC 
simulation method is introduced in this paper to reduce the 
computation burden. The generation process of low-difference 
Sobol sequence in QMC simulation is given in [7]. 
III. UNCERTAINTY AND CORRELATION OF DG OUTPUT 
This paper takes into account the uncertainty and correlation 
of DG output including wind power and photovoltaic power. 
Based on a large number of measurements, KDE is used to 
obtain the PDF of wind speed and solar radiation intensity. 
Considering the correlation of output of DG units, based on the 
Copula theory, a joint probability distribution model can be 
established. The samples of wind speed or solar radiation 
intensity are obtained according to the Copula function and the 
output power of DG units can be calculated. 
A. Uncertainty of DG Output 
Due to the uncertainty of the DG output, the parameter 
estimation method obtains the estimated values of the unknown 
parameters from the sample data based on the assumed PDF. 
However, when the random variable does not obey the 
previously assumed probability distribution, the method has a 
large error. KDE is a non-parametric method for estimating the 
probability distribution of random variables. The selection of 
kernel functions can adapt to the distribution characteristics of 
random variables.

variable x, the KDE of the PDF of the random variable x is

Common Copula functions are Archimedes Copula function 
family and ellipsoid Copula function family. The Archimedes 
Copula function family includes Clayton-Copula, Gumbel-
Copula and Frank-Copula functions. The ellipsoid Copula 
function includes Gaussian-Copula and t-Copula functions[8]. In 
this paper, the most suitable Copula function among the above 
five functions is used to co nstruct the joint probability 
distribution function between different random variables by the 
K-S test. 
Based on the above probability distribution or joint 
probability distribution function of the DG output, the Sobol 
sequence is used to obtain the wind speed or the solar radiation 
intensity. Then, the output power of the wind turbine or 
photovoltaic power plant can be calculated[5].

correlation between the load growth factor depends on the type 
of load. In this paper, we first assume that the load growth factor

V. PROBABILISTIC STATIC VOLTAGE STABILITY 
ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE IN DISTRIBUTION NETWORK 
A procedure of probabilistic static voltage stability 
assessment is established in this paper based on the QMC 
simulation method. The uncertainty and correlation of DG 
output and load growth in distribution network are considered. 
The procedure is given as follows 
(1) According to the measurements of the DG, obtain the 
probability distribution or joint probability distribution of 
the random input variables y1, y2,…,yN by the KDE and 
Copula functions. 
(2) Determine the sampling size n. 
(3) Obtain a sample matrix Y based on the probability 
distribution or the joint probability distribution of the 
random variables y1,y2,…,yN based on QMC simulation. 
(4) Generate sample matrix KL based on normal distribution 
parameters and correlation coefficient matrix of different 
load growth factors kL,1, kL,2,…,kL,m. 
(5) Generate the sample matrix Z of the DG output from the 
sample matrix Y based on the relationship between the DG 
output z1, z2,…,zN and the random variables y1, y2,…,yN. 
(6) Combine the sample matrices  Z  and KL into the sample 
matrix X of the random input variable x in equation (1). 
(7) d=1, let Xd be the d-th column of matrix X. 
(8) Based on the random input variable Xd, calculate the load 
margin of the distribution network by continuous power 
flow. 
(9) d=d+1, if d>n, proceed to the next calculation, otherwise go 
to (8); 
(10) Obtain the probability distribution curve of load margin and 
analyze the operation risk of distribution network.

VI. CASE STUDY 
A. Data 
In this paper, the IEEE 33-bus distribution network [9] is 
tested. The distribution network is connected to the utility grid 
through bus 1 and the reference voltage is 12.66kV. There are 4 
DG units integrated in the distribution network including 2 wind 
turbines, 1 photovoltaic power plant and 1 gas turbine. The wind 
speed and the solar radiation intensity are collected within one 
year in a certain area of western China. The rated capacity of the 
wind turbine is 280kW. The cut-in, rated and cut-out wind speed 
of wind turbine are 3m/s, 15m/s and 20m/s, respectively. The 
area of the photovoltaic array is 2000m 2 and the photoelectric 
conversion efficiency is 14%. The load growth factor satisfies 
the normal distribution with the mean of 2.5 and the standard 
deviation of 0.25. The correlation coefficient between the same 
type of load is 0.8 and these between the different types of load 
is 0.2, which indicates the correlation. 
In this paper, four cases are studied. Case 1: the random input 
variables are independent. Case 2: the correlation among loads 
is considered, regardless of the correlation of renewable energy. 
Case 3: the correlation of renewable energy is considered, 
regardless of the correlation between loads. Case 4: the 
correlation of renewable energy and loads are both considered.

B. Comparison of sampling methods 
The distribution network with 2 wind turbines and 1 gas 
turbine is illustrated in Fig. 1. In  case 4, the Copula function is 
used to establish the joint probability distribution function of 
wind speed. Through the K-S test method, the most suitable 
Copula function is selected to describe the joint probability 
distribution between wind turbines. The infinite norm between 
the five common Copula functions and the empirical distribution 
function in the K-S test is represented as d=||·|| ∞ , as shown in 
Table 1.  
By comparison, the Gumbel-Copula function with the best 
fitting degree is selected to describe the joint probability 
distribution between wind speeds. The joint probability density 
function and joint cumulative probability distribution function 
between wind turbine 1 and 2 are shown in Fig. 2. 
Based on the joint probability distribution between the wind 
speeds, 500 wind speed samples are obtained by SRS method 
and Sobol sequences, respectively. The load margin is 
calculated using continuous power flow. The computation time 
for different sampling methods, the mean and standard deviation 
σ of the load margin are shown in Table 2. Meanwhile, the PDFs 
of the load margin is shown in Fig. 3. 
According to the Table 2 and Fig. 3, the results of QMC 
simulation based on Sobol sequence under the same sampling 
times are closer to the referen ce value. With the same sample 
size, the QMC based on Sobol sequence can obtain more 
accurate results compared with SRS method. Therefore, the 
QMC based on Sobol sequence is utilized to perform a 
probabilistic static voltage stability assessment.

According to the PDFs and CDFs in Fig. 4 and Fig. 5, it can 
be seen that the correlation among loads has a great influence on 
the probability distribution of the load margin. The correlation 
mainly affects the variance of the PDF of load margin. 
Meanwhile, the influence of correlation among wind power on 
the probability distribution of load margin is much smaller than 
that among loads. The reason is that the proportion of wind 
power output in the distribution network system is relatively 
small in this paper, and thus, its correlation has a relatively small 
impact on the probability distribution of the load margin. 
D. DG configuration analysis 
In the 33-bus distribution network system of Fig. 1, a 
photovoltaic power plant is integrated in this network with three 
modes. Meanwhile, the output power of photovoltaic cell and 
the wind turbine are independent. Taking into account the 
uncertainty of the solar radiatio n intensity the three modes are 
given as follows, mode 1: the photovoltaic cell does not access 
to the distribution network; mode 2: the photovoltaic cell is

photovoltaic cell is accessed to the distribution network at bus 
18. The PDFs and CDFs of the load margin are obtained 
respectively, as shown in Fig. 6 and Fig. 7. Moreover, the mean 
and standard deviation of the load margins with the three modes 
are shown in Table 3. 
From Fig. 6 and Fig. 7, it can be seen that compared with the 
mode 1, the PDFs and CDFs of mode 2 and mode 3 are both 
shifted to the right. Further, combined with Table 3, the mean of 
load margin is improved and the static voltage stability is 
enhanced in the distribution network. Meanwhile, compared the 
mode 2 and mode 3, it can be seen that the mean of the load 
margin is more greatly increased in mode 3. Therefore, the 
connection location of the DG units which is selected reasonably 
can further enhance the voltage stability of the distribution 
network.

VII. CONCLUSION 
In this paper, considering the uncertainty and correlation of 
renewable energy and loads, a probabilistic static voltage 
stability assessment method for distribution network is proposed. 
The probability distribution of DG output power is obtained by 
non-parametric KDE method. Meanwhile, the Copula function 
is used to establish the joint probability distribution for the 
correlated DG output power. The samples of random input 
variables are obtained based on QMC simulation, and the load 
margin is calculated by continuous power flow. Through the 
simulation of the distribution network system, the main 
conclusions are given as follows: 
(1) The QMC simulation based on Sobol sequence can improve 
the calculation efficiency and guarantee accuracy of results. 
Compared with the SRS-based MCS, it is more suitable for 
the probabilistic static voltage stability assessment of the 
distribution network. 
(2) The correlation among DG and loads has a significant 
impact on the static voltage stability of the distribution 
network. 
(3) The reasonable configuration for DG units is beneficial to 
improve the static voltage stability of system.
